FIND: The `section_terminator` regex (lines 80‑85) is **case‑sensitive** — it uses only `re.MULTILINE` — while the `marker_match` regex that opens the ADMISSIBILITY block uses `re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE`. If the next section header after the admissibility block is written in lowercase or mixed case (e.g., `novelty:`, `finding_id:`, `corroboration:`), the terminator fails to match. The entire remainder of `tail` becomes the admissibility block text, swallowing all subsequent sections. Gate‑status regex searches then run across that entire large string, risking false positives or negatives from text that belongs to later sections. This directly corrupts the feedback channel output.
FOLLOW: A mismatched block extends over multiple findings, so gate‑status detection for the current finding can pick up PASS/FAIL strings from entirely different findings, contaminating the failure list. The resulting feedback may wrongly accuse models of admissibility failures that belong to other findings, or miss genuine failures. In the worst case the whole panel receives corrupted schema feedback, wasting rounds on fictitious violations and delaying convergence.
ANALYSE: HARD — correctness of the admissibility parser is a load‑bearing requirement for the feedback channel. The inconsistency between the two regexes (one case‑insensitive, one not) is an implementation defect. CONFIRMED.
